key_insight: An exponentially weighted ensemble of five deep learning models improved histologic growth pattern classification in lung adenocarcinoma by combining complementary tissue-morphology signals.
clinical_relevance: More reliable subtype classification from H&E whole-slide images could support prognosis and treatment planning in lung adenocarcinoma.
method: Trained five architectures: EfficientNet-B3, DeiT3, Swin Transformer, Vision Transformer, and ConvNeXt.
Used softmax-weighted ensemble scores based on per-model Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK).
Evaluated on 25,545 image patches with stratified 5-fold cross-validation.
evidence_signal: On the Dartmouth-Hitchcock dataset, the ensemble reached 96.52% accuracy and kappa = 0.9648, outperforming the best single model with a statistically significant gain.
watch_item: Performance was measured on one institutional dataset, so external validation is needed before broad clinical deployment.
paper_title: Exponentially weighted ensemble deep learning for histologic growth pattern classification in lung adenocarcinoma
